cells: $150-250 retail; BOM ceiling under review (research estimate $100-130)

rows.label: Keys
cells: small keys, too small to play comfortably

cells: pocket size (measure yours on the Layouts page)
about 300-360 x 190-200 mm, from the layout calculator

microSD, minutes to hours, 44.1/48 kHz stereo

rows.label: Sequencer

pattern + song, per-step parameter locks (to design)

rows.label: Polyphony
cells: Otter 4 voices; drum voices per pad

rows.label: Audio I/O
cells: stereo in and out, built-in mic and speaker

rows.label: MIDI
cells: TRS-A in/out, USB-C device, sync in/out

rows.label: Power
cells: Li-ion cell + USB-C charge, 6 h target

wants: Keys a hand can actually play, and pads as well as keys: the FM-1 has neither.
Sample time that is measured in minutes, not seconds (the FM-1 holds about 4 s).
Stereo 48 kHz samples and a clean output path.
A real MIDI port (TRS-A) as well as USB, plus a sync option.
Pads or keys that feel good: velocity and pressure, the thing that sells the EP-133 and Chompi.
Open, documented firmware so engines can be added without a hardware change.
A BOM that leaves room for a $150-250 price; Chompi at $599 shows the ceiling, the FM-1 at about $70 shows the floor.
